Released: 20 August 2026

EDB Postgres Distributed (PGD) 5.9.5 includes only bug fixes focused on improving stability and reliability. For a list of known issues, see [Known issues](/pgd/current/known_issues/).

## Security Fixes

<table class="table w-100"><thead><tr><th>Component</th><th>Version</th><th>Description</th><th width="10%">Addresses</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>PGD Proxy</td><td>5.9.5</td><td><details><summary>Updated PGD Proxy Go dependencies to address known vulnerabilities.</summary><hr/><p>Updated <code>golang.org/x/crypto</code>, <code>github.com/jackc/pgx/v5</code>, and related transitive dependencies to their latest patch versions to resolve known CVEs.</p>
</details></td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>


## Bug Fixes

<table class="table w-100"><thead><tr><th>Component</th><th>Version</th><th>Description</th><th width="10%">Addresses</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>BDR</td><td>5.9.5</td><td><details><summary>Fixed node-join failure caused by an under-sized replication origin estimate during catch-up.</summary><hr/><p>The function <code>bdr.get_min_required_replication_slots()</code> previously ignored the temporary catch-up subscription active during a node join, so joining a cluster sized to the reported minimum exhausted <code>max_replication_slots</code> and failed. The estimate now accounts for the catch-up subscription, and a new <code>bdr.get_min_required_active_replication_origins()</code> function returns the matching estimate for PostgreSQL 18's separate <code>max_active_replication_origins</code> limit.</p>
</details></td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>BDR</td><td>5.9.5</td><td><details><summary>Fixed a crash caused by a race between a joining and a parting node.</summary><hr/><p>A joining node sometimes reached the <code>PART_CATCHUP</code> phase of a concurrent node part before it had created a replication origin for the parting node, crashing the manager or writer process when it tried to access the missing origin. PGD now creates the origin in this case, and removes it automatically once the parting node reaches the <code>PARTED</code> state.</p>
</details></td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>BDR</td><td>5.9.5</td><td><details><summary>Fixed a crash on dynamic partition creation for <code>HASH</code> and <code>LIST</code> subpartitions.</summary><hr/><p>Creating a dynamic interval partition with <code>HASH</code> or <code>LIST</code> subpartitions crashed the originating node, and once fixed, produced duplicate partition names that looped until the server ran out of memory. The partition-naming hook is now strategy-aware, producing a unique, deterministic name for each partition across all nodes.</p>
</details></td><td>61769</td></tr>
<tr><td>PGD Proxy</td><td>5.9.5</td><td><details><summary>Fixed PGD Proxy packages not upgrading to 5.9.5.</summary><hr/><p>The 5.9.5 PGD Proxy package had a lower epoch than 5.9.4, so package managers treated it as older and skipped the upgrade. The epoch is now set correctly.</p>
</details></td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>Utilities</td><td>5.9.5</td><td><details><summary>Fixed <code>bdr_init_physical</code> potentially failing during a large physical join.</summary><hr/><p><code>bdr_init_physical</code> previously had a fixed ceiling on how long it would wait for the joining node to catch up and promote, which could be exceeded when replaying WAL from a large base backup. The command now waits without a fixed timeout by default, reporting replay progress along the way. Set <code>PGCTLTIMEOUT</code> to bound the wait instead.</p>
</details></td><td>63142</td></tr>
<tr><td>BDR</td><td>5.9.5</td><td><details><summary>Fixed <code>ALTER PROFILE</code> replication failure on witness nodes when a password verify function is set.</summary><hr/><p>On EDB Postgres Advanced Server (EPAS), witness nodes don't replicate non-role database objects, so replicating <code>ALTER PROFILE</code> with a <code>PASSWORD_VERIFY_FUNCTION</code> failed on witness nodes with a <code>function does not exist</code> error. PGD now skips executing the function on witness nodes, since it already ran on the originating node.</p>
</details></td><td>61289</td></tr>
<tr><td>BDR</td><td>5.9.5</td><td><details><summary>Protect against creating a Default partition on an autopartitioned table.</summary><hr/><p>Autopartition doesn't support a Default partition. DDL that attempted to create one on an autopartitioned table is now rejected instead of leaving the table in an inconsistent state.</p>
</details></td><td>61462</td></tr>
<tr><td>BDR</td><td>5.9.5</td><td><details><summary>Fixed <code>bdr.switch_node_group</code> incorrectly succeeding in a mixed-version cluster during a rolling upgrade.</summary><hr/><p><code>bdr.switch_node_group</code> was previously allowed even when the cluster hadn't yet reached the required Raft protocol version during a rolling upgrade. It's now permitted only after the cluster reaches the required protocol version, with a clear error otherwise.</p>
</details></td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>PGD CLI</td><td>5.9.5</td><td><details><summary>Fixed <code>pgd replication show</code> erroring out on a subscription with a NULL LSN.</summary><hr/><p><code>pgd replication show</code> failed instead of reporting a subscription that hasn't made progress and has a NULL LSN. The command now reports these no-progress subscriptions without erroring out.</p>
</details></td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>BDR</td><td>5.9.5</td><td><details><summary>Fixed commit decisions never being cleaned up for certain workloads after repeated timeouts.</summary><hr/><p>Under certain workloads, the commit-decision store's maintenance pass could time out repeatedly without ever fully cataloging its backlog, leaving some commit decisions uncleaned. Maintenance now performs a final no-timeout cleanup pass after multiple timeouts, ensuring all commit decisions are eventually cleaned up.</p>
</details></td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>BDR</td><td>5.9.5</td><td><details><summary>Fixed resource leaks in <code>bdr.ri_fkey_on_del_trigger</code>.</summary><hr/><p>The <code>bdr.ri_fkey_on_del_trigger</code> trigger function left a relation, a tuple descriptor, and a snapshot open every time it ran, logging <code>resource was not closed</code> warnings on every node. The function now closes these resources correctly.</p>
</details></td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>
